Spring 2027 exchange: Ashworth University, Boston (J-1 exchange student)
- Home: Westbridge University, BSc Economics, year 2. Exchange coordinator: Ada Green.
- Programme dates on my Ashworth admission: 13 January 2027 to 21 May 2027.
- Housing: applied for Scholar Court (single room).
- I want to take Spanish (LANG110) while I am there.

- Rules: Westbridge exchange handbook 2026-27 and Ashworth's J-1 registration rules, both in this folder.
- Keep costs down: travel and fees come out of my savings.

Westbridge University Study Abroad Office
Exchange handbook 2026-27: semester exchanges (applies to exchanges that start in autumn 2026 or spring 2027)

1. Load. Register for courses worth 30 ECTS, the same as a Westbridge semester. At a US partner this is 15 US semester credits (1 US credit = 2 ECTS). Do not register for more than 18 US credits.
2. Compulsory modules. Year 2 Economics students take the approved partner equivalents of ECN2001 Intermediate Microeconomics and ECN2010 Quantitative Methods II. At Ashworth University these are ECON210 and STAT201.
3. Subject credits. At least 9 of the 15 US credits must be economics or statistics (ECON or STAT) courses at 200 level or above; the compulsory equivalents count.
4. Level. Courses below 200 level do not count towards the 30 ECTS, except one language course.
5. Languages. At most one language course per semester.
6. Grading. Take every course for a letter grade; pass/fail or audit results cannot be converted.
7. Learning Agreement. Every course must be approved by your exchange coordinator on your Learning Agreement before you register for it. Changes after registration need the coordinator's approval within two weeks.
8. Records. Your coordinator needs course codes, titles, credits and registration status only. Do not send passports, student finance or bank documents to academic staff.

Westbridge University Study Abroad Office
Exchange handbook 2025-26: semester exchanges (superseded on 1 August 2026 by the 2026-27 edition)

1. Load. Register for courses worth at least 24 ECTS. At a US partner this is 12 US semester credits.
2. Compulsory modules. Take the approved partner equivalent of ECN2001 Intermediate Microeconomics.
3. Level. Courses below 200 level do not count, except language courses.
4. Grading. Electives may be taken pass/fail where the partner allows it.
5. Learning Agreement. Your coordinator approves your courses before you register.

Ashworth University, International Exchange Office
Spring 2027 registration rules for J-1 exchange students

1. Full-time enrollment. J-1 students must be registered for at least 12 credits each semester. Only courses you are registered in count; waitlisted courses do not.
2. Online courses. J-1 exchange students may take at most one online course (up to 3 credits) per semester, and it counts towards the 12 credits only if the rest of the schedule is in person.
3. Maximum load. 18 credits.
4. Prerequisites. Transfer credit from your home university is on your Ashworth record and satisfies prerequisites. Exchange students may not override a prerequisite themselves; an override needs the instructor's signed permission form.
5. Grading. Exchange students take courses for a letter grade unless their home university allows otherwise.
6. Timing. Exchange registration opens on Thursday 12 November 2026 at 09:00 Eastern Time and closes on Friday 20 November 2026.
7. Pre-registration. Courses your home university asked us to pre-register stay on your schedule unless your home coordinator asks us in writing to remove them.

Hi Noah,

Thanks for the draft. Two things before you redo it once Ashworth publishes the spring schedule:
- ECON301 won't work: Ashworth requires STAT201 and ECON210 first, and you'd be taking STAT201 in the same term.
- Please use the 2026-27 handbook. The load went up to 30 ECTS this year and the subject-credit rule is new; the 2025-26 one is out of date.

Ada

Ada Green | Exchange Coordinator, School of Economics | Westbridge University

Ashworth has confirmed your place for spring 2027 and has pre-registered you in STAT201 (CRN 21001), the approved equivalent of ECN2010 Quantitative Methods II.

Please build the rest of your Learning Agreement from Ashworth's spring schedule under the 2026-27 handbook and send me the proposed list (course code, section and CRN for each) by Friday 6 November. I've held Thursday 5 November, 11:00-11:30 (UK time) for a video call if you want to go through it. Put it in your diary if you'd like it.

Ada

advisor_notes.text: Pre-registered in STAT201 (CRN 21001) at Westbridge's request; Westbridge equivalent of ECN2010. Transfer credit ECON101, STAT101 and MATH120 posted from Westbridge Year 1.

course_reviews.text: Lots of speaking practice in pairs, small class. Great if you have never done Spanish.
Weekly problem sets, curve is fair. Section 002 is in the big Hale Hall room.
Brilliant lectures, two essays and a final. The morning section fills up last.
Self-paced online modules, but the Sunday deadlines are strict.
Fun topics; the two online exams are proctored by webcam.
Lots of R coding. Office hours help.
